name: Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Disorder Due to a Point Mutation of Mitochondrial DNA

criteria.description: Presence of multisystem clinical features consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction including neurological and muscular symptoms
Demonstration of impaired oxidative phosphorylation enzyme activity in muscle biopsy or other tissues
Identification of a pathogenic point mutation in mitochondrial DNA associated with oxidative phosphorylation defects
Characteristic brain MRI abnormalities such as basal ganglia lesions or cerebral atrophy
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical features plus biochemical evidence and genetic confirmation of mitochondrial DNA point mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

searchTerms: muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
abnormal muscle fibers with red staining

common.notes: Elevated lactate levels from defective oxidative phosphorylation

occasional.notes: May present as hypertrophic or dilated forms
Cerebellar involvement leading to coordination difficulties
Ranges from mild to severe dementia

rare.notes: Progressive vision loss due to optic nerve degeneration

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Abnormal oxidative phosphorylation enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia calcifications or lesions
Cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on neuroimaging
genetic: Detection of pathogenic point mutations in mitochondrial DNA (e.g., m.3243A>G, m.8344A>G)
Heteroplasmy levels correlating with disease severity
other: Muscle biopsy revealing ragged-red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase-negative fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily optic neuropathy with acute/subacute vision loss
Specific mtDNA mutations distinct from oxidative phosphorylation point mutations
Large-scale mtDNA deletions rather than point mutations
Onset before age 20 with pigmentary retinopathy and cardiac conduction defects
Progressive external ophthalmoplegia common but accompanied by additional systemic features

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia with multisystem involvement
Elevated lactate levels unexplained by other causes
Family history of mitochondrial disease or maternal inheritance pattern
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003;348(26):2656-2668.
Gorman GS, et al. Mitochondrial diseases. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2016;2:16080.
Orphanet: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder due to a point mutation of mitochondrial DNA. ORPHA:254776.
